body:
# the contributor audit: actual shell signatures and the selected tilt switch

Source: `candidate 046287857a52d424`.
Result: PASS for Sections1--5. The exact109-check verifier was rerun PASS.

The uniform shell law uses the correct radial density d r^(d-1)/tau and
the actual cone probability about an interior center. The common radial
variable preserves all shell marginals. Its outputs need belong only to
the ORIGINAL target fiber, which is all the indicator implication needs.
The source now correctly invokes the pointwise hitting-cost proof rather
than assuming these nonconvex shells satisfy convex-source hypotheses.
Boundary-null assumptions justify the joint signature limit by dominated
convergence and are explicit limitations. The loss coefficients scale
by d, not by an untracked shell probability.

The exact proper circuit response is q=-sum theta_j L_j, with actual
theta proportional to rho/S. Its sign and threshold beta d A are correct.
One compatible deformation must pay each chosen witness separately;
averaging the witness tests is not justified or claimed. Supporting
branches and new centers are not silently inserted into this formula.

The five rectangle halfwidth sequences have exactly the stated second
differences after contracting bases-1,1,2. Positivity and concavity hold
for epsilon<1/7. Central reflection treats the original nonvertical caps;
closed pure-base caps through the origin also capture at least half the
mass, retaining their boundary fiber. Every source/output line in the
test is null for its cone law. Each of the two crossing intervals has
cone probability1/160, giving loss-credit gain1/20. The raw coareas15,15,20
and response weights2/7,2/7,3/7 are consistent under unit normalization.

Adding common integer tilt10 leaves the target signatures unchanged but
makes the positive-base traces full and negative-base traces empty.
The true losses are43 in each cap while beta times total removal is39.
The exact changing masses and normalized strict improvement follow as
printed. The middle plane is covered by the selected positive circuit;
the explicit other-base covers have masses at most51/4 (endpoints2) and
remain slack throughout the stated epsilon range. Thus the comparison
really decreases global maximum normalized depth, not just one source.
The new proper coareas4,4,6 yield weights3/10,3/10,2/5. Their target-only
adaptive bound1753/100 fails to capture the actual source surplus.

This calibration is above OC and proves no universal payment, but it is
an actual selection/deformation example: changing mixed cap tilts can
matter while preserving every target signature in the proposed coupling.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
